text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with one quote of every variant type for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 reporting year, the Harrowmere Community Listening Centre delivered 1,240 individual counselling sessions to residents of Velden District. Of the 312 new clients registered, 64 percent were women and roughly one in five were adolescents. Our six lay counsellors completed forty hours of refresher training in problem-solving therapy. Waiting times fell from three weeks to nine days after we opened a second room at the Tannery Road site. However, the planned peer support groups for older men did not start, because no suitable facilitator could be recruited before October. We remain grateful to the Linwell Foundation for its continued support and flexibility.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring visit, Q3 2024: Field staff from Clearspring Water Trust inspected 18 boreholes and 142 household latrines across the Ombare and Kessit sub-counties. Fourteen boreholes were fully functional, while four had broken handpumps awaiting spare parts. Average queuing time at functional points was 12 minutes, down from 35 minutes at baseline. Water committees in Kessit collected user fees in every month of the quarter. Handwashing stations were present at 61% of latrines visited, but soap wasn't available at most of them. The team did not observe any open defecation near the school compounds. A follow-up visit is scheduled for 15 January 2025.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Ubuhle Home Care Programme, conducted in March 2022, found that 87 community caregivers were actively visiting clients in Nkalane and Sithebe wards. Caregivers made an average of six home visits per client each month, exceeding the target of four. Clients reported that caregivers helped them collect antiretroviral refills and reminded them of clinic appointments. Viral load suppression among enrolled clients rose to 78 percent, compared with 59 percent at baseline. However, the stipend system was not functioning as designed, and several caregivers had gone two months without payment. The evaluators recommend that the programme should never rely on a single disbursement channel.

passages.source_passage: In its second year, the Shantipur Mothers' Outreach Project extended monthly clinic camps to 23 villages in the Ralgaon block. Trained outreach workers registered 1,068 pregnant women, and 72% of them completed at least four antenatal check-ups. Facility births among registered women increased from 41% in 2022 to 58% in 2023. Each camp offered blood pressure screening, iron supplements and counselling on newborn danger signs. No maternal deaths were recorded among registered women during the year. Postnatal visits within two days of birth remained low, and we did not reach our target for the Dhanpur cluster. We thank the Ardent Health Fund for enabling this work.

passages.source_passage: Throughout the 2023–2024 school year, the Kolani Schools Nourish Initiative served a hot midday meal to 9,450 pupils in 37 primary schools across the Dargou region. Meals combined locally grown millet, cowpeas and fortified oil purchased from 210 women's cooperatives. Average attendance rose to 91 percent, and head teachers reported fewer pupils leaving school at midday. Girls' enrolment in grade one grew by eleven percent compared with the previous year. Deliveries were interrupted for three weeks in February when the main road flooded, and pupils in Tiéssa did not receive meals during that period. No school reported a food safety incident.

passages.source_passage: Board update, 4 June 2024: The Sundar Valley net campaign is now 80% complete. Distribution teams have handed out 46,200 long-lasting insecticidal nets to 19,800 households, using the village registers verified in April. Hang-up checks in a sample of 400 homes found nets correctly installed over sleeping spaces in three out of four cases. Stock losses have been minimal, and no nets have been reported for sale in local markets. The remaining two districts were not reached in May because the delivery truck broke down. The programme team expects to finish distribution by the end of July, within the approved budget.

passages.source_passage: Board update, September 2023. The Marrowbay Coastal Alert Programme has now installed siren towers in 12 of the 15 target fishing villages along the Selka shoreline. During the August drill, 2,300 residents reached designated shelters within 25 minutes of the first alert. Village volunteers relayed warnings by megaphone to households that the sirens could not reach. The SMS alert system did not perform well: only 54% of registered phones received the test message. Our technical partner believes the gateway, not the network, was at fault. We have never conducted a drill at night, and the committee recommends one before the cyclone season begins in November.

passages.source_passage: Over the twelve months to March 2024, the Openway Inclusion Project provided 486 assistive devices, including wheelchairs, hearing aids and white canes, to residents of Calder and Brisk counties. Each device was fitted by a trained technician, and 93% of recipients were still using their device at the six-month follow-up. Ramps and handrails were added to 14 health posts and nine schools. Local councils have not yet adopted the accessibility standards we drafted with disabled persons' organisations, although two councils have scheduled a vote. We never charged recipients for devices or repairs. Demand far exceeds supply, and the waiting list now stands at 310 people.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation covers the first 30 months of the Greenfurrow Farmer Field School Network in Lusenje and Mbati districts. By June 2023, 64 field schools had been established, with a combined membership of 1,720 farmers, of whom 58 percent were women. Members who adopted mulching and intercropping reported maize yields roughly 40 percent higher than non-members. Facilitators were drawn from among the farmers themselves, which kept costs low. The evaluation team found that the seed bank component had not worked: no school had stored enough seed to replant after the 2022 drought. Market linkages remain weak, and few groups sell collectively.

passages.source_passage: In 2023 the Lanternhill Evening Literacy Network ran 52 classes in church halls, mosques and community centres across the Pelham Flats estates. A total of 780 adults enrolled, and 61% completed the full 36-week course. Learners who finished the course could read a simple newspaper article and fill in a bank form without help. Most learners were women aged between 30 and 55. Attendance dropped sharply in December, and the network did not hold classes during the two-week holiday break. Volunteer tutors were never paid, but each received a travel allowance. We hope to open eight new classes next year if funding allows.
